## Introduction {.unlisted}

Welcome to [BIOL2022 Biology Experimental Design and Analysis](https://canvas.sydney.edu.au/courses/67437), known as BEDA. This unit is about designing biological studies, analysing data, and evaluating evidence.

The handbook contains the unit information, practical materials, assessment guidance, and weekly resources used throughout the semester. Canvas remains the official location for announcements and submission links.

::: {.callout-note}
A basic understanding of introductory statistics is assumed. If you need a refresher, see [Am I ready for BEDA?](prerequisites.qmd).
:::

## Using this handbook {.unlisted}

Use this handbook alongside Canvas. In the HTML version, use the sidebar to move between practicals, assessments, and supporting resources. In the PDF version, use the table of contents and internal links.

For general expectations and course structure, see [Unit Information](unit-information.qmd). For assessment instructions, marking guidance, and submission details, see [Assessments](assessments/assessments.qmd).

## Unit structure {.unlisted}

BEDA is organised into three modules.

| Module | Weeks | Focus |
|---|---:|---|
| Fundamentals | 1-5 | Design, data, linear models, and assumptions |
| Univariate experiments | 6-8 | Models for experiments with one response variable |
| Multivariate experiments | 9-13 | Multivariate biological data analysis |

## Assessment overview {.unlisted}

The assessment pages provide the full instructions and marking criteria. The table below is only a summary of the major assessment tasks.

| Assessment | Module | Weight |
|---|---:|---:|
| Early Feedback Task | Module 1 | 5% |
| Evaluation Quiz | Module 1 | 10% |
| Report 1 | Module 2 | 25% |
| Report 2 | Module 3 | 20% |

See [Assessments](assessments/assessments.qmd) for complete details.
